main_text.l: honorem, magno cum augmento honoris poteft sine ulla compensatione emitti; ut cum Rex aliquis servo suo emittit debitum aliquot millium florenorum. Hoc debitum ut non laedeat Majestatem Regis, ita salva Majestate remitti potuit.

Si vero debita laedant honorem & Majestatem creditoris, ejusque naturae & gloriae ex diametro adversentur, certè non possunt sine satisfactione, libero quodam ductu voluntatis, remitti. Alia autem debita sunt peccata; utpote, quae aeternae voluntatis divinae regulam infringunt, eíque adversantur: ita ut salva Dei justitia & rectitudine, sine poena expiari non possint.

Hinc adeò est, quod quidam distinguant debitum in Externum & Internum. Externum debitum dicunt civile illud, ad quod bona tantum fortunae contingunt, non autem bona ipsa interiora, sive virtutem ejus, cui debetur, & tale affirmant remitti posse salva justitia sine satisfactione. page.notes: The faint "305" at the upper right is not a printed page number (the page is numbered 185) and was left out. The first marginal note is hard to read; "dens aut ut" and "laedens," are my best reading, and "ut" is doubtful. The second note is partly faded. Printed words in the text such as "libero" and "eíque" are copied as they appear. The final line ends in "virtu-" with a printed hyphen, so it is kept as text, not as a catchword.
